context.name: Quantum Leap
context.description: My friend took the quantum leap and purchased a quantum computer with two qubits. They mentioned using a quantum logic gate to input the flag and they gave me the computers output. I have been stuck and Can NOT figure out the flag.

content: The output file may contain quantum state amplitudes or measurement results; inspecting its type and contents will show the format.
The file is ASCII text; viewing its contents will reveal the quantum output format (likely measurement counts or amplitudes).

The scrambling is a fixed bit permutation plus XOR applied to each byte (a qubit-gate-like bit shuffle); brute-force all 8! permutations and 256 XOR keys and keep those that decode to flag{...}.
The output is 20 ASCII characters that look scrambled, not a plain flag. Next I'll test whether a fixed bit permutation plus XOR key maps them back to a `flag{...}` string.

The byte transform may be a composition of standard bijections (rotation, Gray code, bit-reverse, add/sub, XOR); search compositions for one that decodes to flag{.
The first brute force (bit permutation plus XOR) found nothing, so I'll widen the search to rotations, Gray codes, bit reversal, add/subtract, and their compositions.

The gate acts on 2-bit groups (two qubits) or the key depends on position; test 4-symbol permutations per 2-bit group plus per-index XOR/add before checking for flag{.
Still no match. I'll try 2-bit symbol permutations and position-dependent transforms (XOR or add with index), since the 2-qubit framing suggests operations on bit pairs.

Swapping the 2-bit symbols 2 and 3 (permutation 0,1,3,2, i.e. a CNOT-like gate on each 2-bit group) with no XOR key decodes the output to a readable flag{...} string.
The 2-bit symbol permutation (0,1,3,2) with XOR key 0 decodes the output to a clean, readable `flag{4_qu4ntum_g4t3}`, which matches the leetspeak theme. Submitting it.
